Aspatial concentration measures for places

Source: R/seg_measures.R
seg_measures.Rd

Summarizes how a group is spread across the census blocks of each place, or of any other unit. Every measure compares the group with everyone else in the unit (the "rest").

Usage

seg_measures(blocks, by, group, total)

Arguments

blocks

A data frame or sf object with one row per block, such as the output of seg_blocks(). Geometry, if present, is ignored.

by

<tidy-select> Column or columns identifying the unit, such as place_geoid. Blocks with a missing value in any by column are dropped.

group, total

<data-masking> Block counts of the group and of the whole population. group must not exceed total.

Value

A tibble with one row per unit: the by columns, n_blocks, pop_total, pop_group, group_share, dissimilarity, isolation, exposure, and majority_share.

Details

For a unit with blocks \(i = 1, \dots, n\), write \(g_i\) for the group count, \(t_i\) for the total, \(r_i = t_i - g_i\) for the rest, and \(G\) and \(R\) for the sums of \(g_i\) and \(r_i\).

  • group_share is the group's share of the unit's population.

  • dissimilarity is \(\frac{1}{2} \sum_i |g_i / G - r_i / R|\): the share of the group that would have to move to another block for every block to match the unit's composition.

  • isolation is \(\sum_i (g_i / G)(g_i / t_i)\): the group's share of the block the average group member lives in.

  • exposure is \(\sum_i (g_i / G)(r_i / t_i)\): the rest's share of the block the average group member lives in. It equals 1 - isolation.

  • majority_share is the share of the group living in blocks where it is more than half of the population.

Blocks with no population add nothing to any measure. A measure that divides by \(G\) or \(R\) is NA when that sum is zero.

See also

seg_clusters() for a spatial measure.

Examples

blocks <- data.frame(
  place = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b"),
  latino = c(40, 10, 0, 5, 5),
  total = c(50, 50, 20, 10, 10)
)
seg_measures(blocks, by = place, group = latino, total = total)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 9
#>   place n_blocks pop_total pop_group group_share dissimilarity isolation
#>   <chr>    <int>     <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>         <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 a            3       120        50       0.417         0.657      0.68
#> 2 b            2        20        10       0.5           0          0.5 
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: exposure <dbl>, majority_share <dbl>
